chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, from Abu al-Harith, who said:
I asked him, meaning al-Rida (peace be upon him), about the four rak'at after Maghrib when traveling; the camel hurries me so I cannot pray on the ground. He said: 'Yes, pray them on the camel.'
ai.seo_question: How to perform voluntary prayers while traveling if you are in a hurry and cannot get off your camel?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the permissibility of performing the four voluntary rak'at after Maghrib while mounted, specifically addressing the practical constraint of being hurried by the camel's movement. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of ease (taysir) in travel, allowing the traveler to maintain spiritual continuity without the burden of dismounting, provided the prayer's essential conditions are met. This ruling is particularly significant in classical contexts where travel conditions were often more arduous than modern equivalents.
